- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism bias.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike (e.g., +10%+ above 30d mean), reduce peak by 10–15% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome over 30d, adjust downward bias by 2–5% per 10d horizon to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.25–0.67) and forecast deviates >5% from true, apply smoothing: average 3d prior + 3d future to reduce noise.  
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is >10% above forecast, assume sentiment is bullish — adjust next forecast upward by 2–3% to reflect momentum.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is erratic, apply low-pass filter: average 5d prior to dampen short-term noise.
